title: Export an MP4 as a MOV File on iPhone
description: Make a separate MOV export from an MP4 on iPhone. Check the receiving app’s file and codec requirements before converting.
direct: If a recipient requires a MOV file, export a new MOV copy from the MP4 and keep the source. Changing the filename extension leaves the file contents as they were.
figureAlt: A phone showing a paused coastal video beside separate large MP4 and MOV file cards.
figureCaption: AI illustration of a source and a separate file copy. The picture does not compare encoding quality.
cards.decision.heading: Ask what must be inside the file
cards.decision.body: MOV is a container. It can hold video, audio and other tracks. A requirement for MOV may come with a separate codec, resolution or frame-rate requirement.
sections.detail-1.heading: If the recipient already accepts MP4
sections.detail-1.body: Try the original first. A different container can help meet a stated requirement. Another encode can take time or change quality, so keep the source if you expect further edits.
sections.detail-2.heading: Check the app’s export scope
sections.detail-2.body: Space Sheep Studio develops Phone Cleaner for iPhone. Its listing includes MOV exports and local HD and 4K video compression. Pro unlocks export tools. A MOV export does not imply a ProRes codec, lossless conversion or unchanged metadata. Check the actual output against the recipient’s written requirements.

steps.step-1.text: Check the receiving app or upload form. Ask whether it needs MOV as a file type or a format such as ProRes inside that file.
steps.step-2.text: Open the MP4 in Phone Cleaner: Photo & Video. Choose its MOV export and review the available settings. Save a separate copy.
steps.step-3.text: Play the copy and check duration, audio and orientation. Inspect its format and codec with a trusted viewer if the recipient specifies both. Test the actual import before you delete any source.
